text:
In the given circuit, the charge on 4 $μ$F capacitor will be :

[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


As V = $\frac{q}{C}$

$\therefore$ V $\propto$ $\frac{1}{C}$

So $\frac{V_{1}}{V_{2}}=\frac{C_{2}}{C_{1}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{V_{1}}{V_{2}}=\frac{6}{4}=\frac{3}{2}$

Also $V_{1} + V_{2} = 10$

$\therefore$ $V_{1} +$ $\frac{2}{3}V_{1} = 10$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{5V_{1}}{3}$ = 10

$\Rightarrow$ $V_{1} = 6 V$

The charge on 4 $μ$F capacitor is $= C_{1}V_{1} = 4$ $\times$ 6 = 24 $μ$C

text:
A particle is moving with speed v = b$\sqrt{x}$ along positive x-axis. Calculate the speed of the particle at
time t = $τ$(assume that the particle is at origin t = 0)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
v = b$\sqrt{x}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{dx}{dt}$ = b$\sqrt{x}$

$\Rightarrow\int\limits _{0}^{x}\frac{dx}{\sqrt{x}}=\int\limits _{0}^{t}bdt$

$\Rightarrow\left [\frac{x^{-\dfrac{1}{2}+1}}{-\frac{1}{2}+1}\right ]_{0}^{x}$ = $b[t]_{0}^{t}$

$\Rightarrow$ $x^{\frac{1}{2}}=\frac{bt}{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $x=\frac{b^{2}t^{2}}{4}$

$\therefore$ v =  $\frac{dx}{dt}$ = $\frac{b^{2}}{4}$ $\times$ 2t = $\frac{b^{2}t}{2}$

When t = $τ$ then speed v  $=\frac{b^{2}τ}{2}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Evening Slot

text:
A transparent cube of side, made of a material of refractive index $μ_{2}$, is immersed in a liquid of refractive
index $μ_{1}$($μ_{1}$ < $μ_{2}$). A ray is incident on the face AB at an angle $θ$(shown in the figure). Total internal
reflection takes place at point E on the face BC.

[IMG]


Then $θ$ must satisfy :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


By Snell’s law at AB

$μ_{1}$ sin $θ$ = $μ_{2}$ sin $α$ 

sin $α$ = $\frac{μ_{1}}{μ_{2}}\sin θ$ ....... (1)

Critical angle at BC,

$μ_{2}$ $\sin  i_{c} =$ $μ_{1}$ $\sin  90^{o}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\sin  i_{c} =$ $\frac{μ_{1}}{μ_{2}}$ ..... (2)

For Total internal reflection to occur,

$90^{o} -$ $α$ $> i_{c}$

Taking sin both side,

$\sin (90^{o} -$ $α) > \sin  i_{c}$

$\Rightarrow$ cos $α$ > $\frac{μ_{1}}{μ_{2}}$   (from equation 2)

$\Rightarrow$ $\sqrt{1-\frac{μ_{1}^{2}}{μ_{2}^{2}}\sin ^{2}θ}$ > $\frac{μ_{1}}{μ_{2}}$   (from equation 1)

Squaring both sides, we get

$1-\frac{μ_{1}^{2}}{μ_{2}^{2}}\sin ^{2}θ$ > $\frac{μ_{1}^{2}}{μ_{2}^{2}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $1-\frac{μ_{1}^{2}}{μ_{2}^{2}}$ > $\frac{μ_{1}^{2}}{μ_{2}^{2}}\sin ^{2}θ$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{μ_{2}^{2}}{μ_{1}^{2}}-1$ > $\sin ^{2}θ$

$\Rightarrow$ sin $θ$ < $\sqrt{\frac{μ_{2}^{2}}{μ_{1}^{2}}-1}$

$\Rightarrow$ $θ<\sin ^{-1}\sqrt{\frac{μ_{2}^{2}}{μ_{1}^{2}}-1}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Evening Slot

text:
Let a total charge 2Q be distributed in a sphere of radius R, with the charge density given by $ρ$(r) = kr, where
r is the distance from the centre. Two charges A and B, of –Q each, are placed on diametrically opposite
points, at equal distance, $a$ from the centre. If A and B do not experience any force, then :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Total charge = 2Q

Charge density $ρ$ = kr

Radius = R

[IMG]

Charge enclosed in the sphere,

$q_{$in} = $\int\limits _{0}^{R}ρdV$

$\Rightarrow$ 2Q = $\int\limits _{0}^{R}kr4πr^{2}dr$

$\Rightarrow$ 2Q = $k4π\int\limits _{0}^{R}r^{3}dr$

$\Rightarrow$ 2Q = $k4π\frac{R^{4}}{4}$

$\Rightarrow$ k = $\frac{2Q}{πR^{4}}$ ........... (1)

Force on charge at A will be due to charge at B and due to force applied by the charge in sphere.

[IMG]


Here $F_{$sphere} = EQ

Using Gauss law, we can find electric field at point A due to sphere,

∮ $\vec{E}.d\vec{A}$ = $\frac{q_{in}}{\in _{0}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $E\left (4πa^{2}\right )$ = $\frac{\int\limits _{0}^{a}ρdV}{\in _{0}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $E\left (4πa^{2}\right )$ = $\frac{k4π\frac{a4}{4}}{\in _{0}}$

$\Rightarrow$ E = $\frac{ka^{2}}{4\in _{0}}$

As on charge A net force is zero then,

 $F_{AB} = F_{$sphere}

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{Q\times Q}{4π\in _{0}(2a)^{2}}$ = $\frac{ka^{2}}{4\in _{0}}$ $\times$ Q

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{Q}{4πa^{2}}=ka^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{Q}{4πa^{2}}=\frac{2Q}{πR^{4}}a^{2}$ [ from equation (1)]

$\Rightarrow$ $8a^{4}=R^{4}$

$\Rightarrow$ $a=8^{-1/4}R$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Evening Slot

text:
A plane electromagnetic wave having a frequency v = 23.9 GHz propagates along the positive z-direction in
free space. The peak value of the Electric Field is 60 V/m. Which among the following is the acceptable
magnetic field component in the electromagnetic wave ?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Since the wave is propagating in positive z-direction

So acceptable magnetic field component will be

$\vec{B}=B_{0}\sin (kz-ωt)\hat{i}$

$\because$ C = $\frac{E_{o}}{B_{o}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $B_{o}=\frac{E_{o}}{C}$ = $\frac{60}{3\times 10^{8}}$ = 2 $\times$ $10^{-7}$

and $ω=2πf$ = 2$π\times$23.9$\times10^{9} = 1.5 × 10^{11} Hz$

and k = $\frac{ω}{c}$ = $\frac{1.5\times 10^{11}}{3\times 10^{8}}$ $= 0.5 × 10^{3}$

Note : When wave is propagating in positive z-direction then sign of kz and $ωt$ should be opposite.

From option you can see only option D can be correct.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Evening Slot

text:
Consider the LR circuit shown in the figure. If the switch S is closed at t = 0 then the amount of charge that
passes through the battery between t = 0 and t = $\frac{L}{R}$
 is :

[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$I=\frac{E}{R}\left (1-e^{-\frac{t}{τ}}\right )$ where $τ$ = $\frac{L}{R}$

We know $dq=Idt$

$\Rightarrow$ $\int\limits _{0}^{Q}dq=\frac{E}{R}\int\limits _{0}^{τ}\left (1-e^{-\frac{t}{τ}}\right )dt$

$\Rightarrow$ Q $=\frac{E}{R}[t]_{0}^{τ}+\frac{E}{R}\times τ\left [e^{-\frac{t}{τ}}\right ]_{0}^{τ}$

         = $\frac{E}{R}τ+\frac{E}{R}τ\left [e^{-1}-1\right ]$

         = $\frac{E}{R}τ+\frac{E}{R}τe^{-1}-\frac{E}{R}τ$

         = $\frac{Eτ}{eR}$

         = $\frac{Eτ}{2.7R}$ [ as e = 2.7 ]

         = $\frac{EL}{2.7R^{2}}$ [as $τ$ = $\frac{L}{R}$ ]

text:
One kg of water, at $20^{o}C$, heated in an electric kettle whose heating element has a mean (temperature
averaged) resistance of 20 $\Omega$. The rms voltage in the mains is 200 V. Ignoring heat loss from the kettle, time
taken for water to evaporate fully, is close to :
[Specific heat of water $= 4200 J/(kg ^{o}C)$, Latent heat of water = 2260 kJ/kg]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
P$\times$t = mS$\Deltat + mL_{v}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{V^{2}}{R}t$ = mS$\Deltat + mL_{v}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{(200)^{2}}{20}t$ = $1\times 4200\times (100-20)$ + $1\times 2260\times 10^{3}$

$\Rightarrow$ 2000t = 336000 + 2260000

$\Rightarrow$ t = 1298 s = 21.6 min $\simeq$ 22 min

A system of three polarizers $P_{1}, P_{2}, P_{3}$ is set up such that the pass axis of $P_{3}$ is crossed with respect to that of $P_{1}$.
The pass axis of $P_{2}$ is inclined at $60^{o}$ to the pass axis of $P_{3}$. When a beam of unpolarized light of intensity $I_{0}$ is
incident on $P_{1}$, the intensity of light transmitted by the three polarizers is I. The ratio ($\frac{I_{0}}{I}$) equals (nearly) :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
When unpolarized light of intensity $I_{0}$ passes through $P_{1}$, then intensity

$I_{1} =$ $\frac{I_{0}}{2}$

as we know, $I = I_{0}$
 $\cos ^{2}θ$

Given that angle between $P_{2}$
 & $P_{3}$
 $= 60^{o}$ and

$P_{1}$
 and $P_{3}$

so angle between $P_{1}$

text:
A diatomic gas with rigid molecules does 10 J of work when expanded at constant pressure. What would be
the heat energy absorbed by the gas, in this process ?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
At constant pressure,

W = P$\Delta$V = nR$\Delta$T

At constant pressure, heat supplied

$Q = nC_{p}\Delta$T

$\frac{W}{Q}=\frac{R}{C_{p}}$

For diatomic gas, $C_{p} =$ $\frac{7}{2}R$

$\therefore$ $\frac{10}{Q}=\frac{R}{\frac{7}{2}R}$

$\Rightarrow$ Q = 10 $\times$ $\frac{7}{2}$ = 35 J

text:
A block of mass 5 kg is (i) pushed in case (A) and (ii) pulled in case (B), by a force F = 20 N, making an
angle of $30^{o}$ with the horizontal, as shown in the figures. The coefficient of friction between the block and
floor is $μ$ = 0.2. The difference between the accelerations of the blocks, in case (B) and case (A) will be :
$(g = 10 ms^{–2})$ 

[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


$N = mg + 20 \sin 30^{o}$

    = 50 + $20\times \frac{1}{2}$

    = 60 N

Limiting friction, $f_{L} =$ $μ$N = 0.2 $\times$ 60 = 12 N

And horizontal force$(F_{x}) = 20 \cos 30^{o} = 10\sqrt{3}$ = 17.32 N

As $F_{x} > f_{L}$, then the block will move with acceleration $a_{A}$.

$a_{A} =$ $\frac{F_{x}-f_{L}}{m_{A}}$ = $\frac{17.32-12}{5}$ = $\frac{5.32}{5}$

[IMG]


$N + 20 \sin 30^{o} = mg$

$N = mg - 20 \sin 30^{o}$

    = 50 - 10 = 40 N

Limiting friction, $f_{L} =$ $μ$N = 0.2 $\times$ 40 = 8 N

And horizontal force$(F_{x}) = 20 \cos 30^{o} = 10\sqrt{3}$ = 17.32 N

As $F_{x} > f_{L}$, then the block will move with acceleration $a_{B}$.

$a_{B} =$ $\frac{F_{x}-f_{L}}{m_{B}}$ = $\frac{17.32-8}{5}$ = $\frac{9.32}{5}$

Difference between acceleration $a_{B} - a_{A} =$ $\frac{9.32}{5}-\frac{5.32}{5}$ = $\frac{4}{5}$ $= 0.8 m/s^{2}$

shunt resistance $R_{A}$ to it and (ii) into a voltmeter of range 0 to $V (V = GI_{0})$ by connecting a series resistance

sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

text:
The number density of molecules of a gas depends on their distance r from the origin as, $n(r)=n_{0}e^{-αr^{4}}$.
Then the total number of molecules is proportional to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Lets take an element hollow sphere of thickness dr

Vol. of element dV = 4$πr^{2}dr$

Total number of molecules,

N = $\int\limits _{0}^{\infty }ndV$

 = $\int\limits _{0}^{\infty }n_{0}e^{-αr^{4}}4πr^{2}dr$

Let $e^{-αr^{4}}$ = t ......................(1)

$\therefore$ $-4αe^{-αr^{4}}r^{3}dr$ = dt

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{dt}{-4αr}=e^{-αr^{4}}r^{2}dr$ .....................(2)

Taking $\ln$ to the both sides of the equation (1), we get

$\ln (t)=-αr^{4}$

$\Rightarrow$ $r=\left (\frac{\ln t}{-α}\right )^{\frac{1}{4}}$ .......(3)

Putting this value of r in equation (2),

$\frac{dt}{-4α\left (\frac{\ln t}{-α}\right )^{\dfrac{1}{4}}}=e^{-αr^{4}}r^{2}dr$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{α^{\dfrac{-3}{4}}dt}{-4(-\ln t)^{\dfrac{1}{4}}}=e^{-αr^{4}}r^{2}dr$

Putting in the integration, we get

N = $n_{0}4π\int\limits _{1}^{0}\frac{α^{\dfrac{-3}{4}}dt}{-4(-\ln t)^{\dfrac{1}{4}}}$

 = $-n_{0}α^{\frac{-3}{4}}π\int\limits _{1}^{0}\frac{dt}{(-\ln t)^{\dfrac{1}{4}}}$

$\therefore$ N $\propto$ $n_{0}α^{\frac{-3}{4}}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Evening Slot

sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

A uniform cylindrical rod of length L and radius r, is made from a material whose Young’s modulus of

longitudinal compressional force F, its length remains unchanged. The coefficient of volume expansion, of
the material of the rod, is (nearly) equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Change in length due to temperature change,

$\Deltal$ = $lα\Delta$T

$\frac{\Delta l}{l}$ = $α$T [ Here  $\Delta$T = T ]

Y = $\frac{\frac{F}{πr2}}{\frac{\Delta l}{l}}$

 = $\frac{\frac{F}{πr2}}{αT}$

$\Rightarrow$ Y = $\frac{F}{πr^{2}αT}$

$\Rightarrow$ $α$ = $\frac{F}{πr^{2}YT}$

We know, The coefficient of volume expansion ($γ$) = 3$α$

$\therefore$ $γ$ = $\frac{3F}{πr^{2}YT}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Evening Slot

text:
A spring whose unstretched length is l has a force constant k. The spring is cut into two pieces of unstretched
lengths $l_{1}$ and $l_{2}$ where, $l_{1} = nl_{2}$ and n is an integer. The ratio $k_{1}/k_{2}$ of the corresponding force constant, $k_{1}$ and
$k_{2}$ will be :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For a spring, k$\timesl$ = constant.

$\therefore$ $k_{1}l_{1}$ $= k_{2}l_{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{k_{1}}{k_{2}}=\frac{l_{2}}{l_{1}}$ = $\frac{l_{2}}{nl_{2}}$ = $\frac{1}{n}$

text:
The ratio of the weights of a body on the Earth’s surface to that on the surface of a planets is 9 : 4. The mass
of the planet is
$\frac{1}{9}$
th of that of the Earth. If 'R' is the radius of the Earth, what is the radius of the planet ?
(Take the planets to have the same mass density)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
W = mg

as m = constant everywhere

$\therefore$ W $\propto$ g

$\frac{g_{E}}{g_{p}}$ = $\frac{9}{4}$

We know,

$g=\frac{GM}{R^{2}}$

$\therefore$ $\frac{g_{E}}{g_{p}}=\frac{M_{E}}{M_{p}}\times \frac{R_{p}^{2}}{R_{E}^{2}}$

$\Rightarrow\frac{9}{4}=\frac{9}{1}\times \frac{R_{p}^{2}}{R_{E}^{2}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{R_{p}}{R_{E}}=\frac{1}{2}$

$R_{p}=\frac{R_{E}}{2}$ = $\frac{R}{2}$ [Here $R_{E} = R$ ]
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Evening Slot

Figure shows a DC voltage regulator circuit, with a Zener diode of breakdown voltage = 6V. If the
unregulated input voltage varies between 10 V to 16 V, then what is maximum Zener current?

solution.body:
[IMG]


$I_{L}=\frac{V_{Z}}{R_{L}}$

= $\frac{6V}{4k\Omega }$ = 1.5 mA

Let input voltage = V

$\therefore$ $\frac{V-V_{Z}}{R_{S}}=I_{s}$

Here maximum input voltage = 16 V

$\therefore$ $\frac{16-6}{2k\Omega }=I_{s}$

$\Rightarrow$ $I_{S} = 5 mA$

$\therefore$ $I_{Z} = I_{S} - I_{L} = 5 - 1.5 = 3.5 mA$

text:
Two particles are projected from the same point with the same speed u such that they have the same range R,
but different maximum heights, $h_{1}$ and $h_{2}$. Which of the following is correct ?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The range of two particles are same, that means angle of projections must be complementary to each other.

So one angle = $θ$ and other one is $= 90^{o} -$ $θ$

R = $\frac{u^{2}\sin 2θ}{g}$ = $\frac{2u^{2}\sin θ\cos θ}{g}$

$\therefore$ $R^{2} =$ $\frac{4u^{4}\sin ^{2}θ\cos ^{2}θ}{g^{2}}$

$h_{1} =$ $\frac{u^{2}\sin ^{2}θ}{2g}$

$h_{2} =$ $\frac{u^{2}\sin ^{2}(90^{o}-θ)}{2g}$ = $\frac{u^{2}\cos ^{2}θ}{2g}$

$h_{1}h_{2} =$ $\frac{u^{4}\sin ^{2}θ\cos ^{2}θ}{4g^{2}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $h_{1}h_{2} =$ $\frac{R^{2}}{16}$

$\Rightarrow$ $R^{2}$
 $= 16 h_{1}h_{2}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Evening Slot
